params.name: q
params.resample_while: q == 0 or q == a or q == 2 * a

stem: A learner sketches $y = {=a}\cos\theta {=signed(q)}$ for $\theta \in [0^\circ, 360^\circ]$ without a table of values, by working out the points of the sketch at $\theta = 0^\circ$, $180^\circ$ and $360^\circ$. Which option gives these three points correctly?
solution: The graph of $y = \cos\theta$ passes through $(0^\circ, 1)$, $(180^\circ, -1)$ and $(360^\circ, 1)$. Multiplying by $a$ stretches these heights (and reflects them in the $x$-axis when $a < 0$); adding $q$ shifts every point vertically by $q$.
At $\theta = 360^\circ$, $\cos\theta$ is $1$ again, so $y = {=a + q}$ again.
The points are $(0^\circ, {=a + q})$, $(180^\circ, {=q - a})$ and $(360^\circ, {=a + q})$.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Getting the reflection in the x-axis the wrong way round
proposed_misconceptions.description: The student swaps the heights at 0 and 360 degrees with the height at 180 degrees: for a negative a they ignore the reflection and start the sketch at its maximum as for y = cos theta (and for a positive a they start it at its minimum), so the two turning heights q + a and q - a trade places.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Leaving out the vertical shift q
proposed_misconceptions.description: The student plots the points of y = a cos theta and forgets to add q, so the sketch is centred on the x-axis instead of on the line y = q.

proposed_misconceptions.label: Shifting the graph the wrong way
proposed_misconceptions.description: The student applies the shift with the wrong sign, subtracting q instead of adding it, so a graph shifted up is drawn shifted down and the other way round.

notes: Standard: the three key points of the sketch (0, 180, 360 degrees), which is how a sketch is built without a table. Every instance has a != 0, q != 0, q != a, q != 2a, which makes the four options differ in their first coordinate pair (checked over the whole parameter space: 56 instances, all with four distinct options). The correct option is a+q, q-a, a+q; the swapped option is the reflection error in either direction. For a < 0 the correct option starts at the minimum. Coordinates are (angle, y). Parent is a basic book item; no book question asks for the key points of a sketch, so this extends the book's amplitude identification to the full a and q effect.
